252: 
253: Required fields: `id: Rddd`, `inputs` (unique proposition IDs), `output` (one
254: N/P ID), `definitions` (direct D references), `rules` (permitted logic-rule
255: names), `locals`, `argument`, and `applications`.
256: 
257: - `locals`: `{symbol, type, scope}` records. Scope identifies a binding inside
258:   this inference; names cannot shadow globals. Two bindings in different
259:   scopes/nodes may use the same spelling. Bound variables of source theorems
260:   can be alpha-renamed and instantiated. Audit actual binding/freshness.
261:   In v2 also require `start`, `end` (inclusive S IDs), `kind` (`arbitrary`,
262:   `definition`, or `witness`), `declaration` (full introduction), `from_inputs`,
263:   `from_local` (prior F IDs) and `objects` (already available objects used to
264:   introduce this one). A witness must have an input/local existence basis.
265:   The checker verifies declared availability/order, not the existence claim's
266:   semantics. Source-bound variables need a legitimate local instantiation.
267:   The `scope` label and inclusive start/end must agree with the prose. Keep an
268:   object live through its last actual use. Establish an existence F in an
269:   earlier S, then choose its witness in a subsequent S; using a newly produced
270:   F as the witness basis in the same paragraph is a forward reference.
271: - `argument`: ordered records `{id: Sddd, text, uses, uses_local, objects,
272:   produces, introduces, discharges}`. S IDs are inference-local and unique. `uses`
273:   lists direct graph inputs used at this point. Local facts established earlier
274:   in the prose do not become graph inputs. The union of `uses` must equal
275:   `inputs`. A citation's presence is not semantic evidence that it was used.
276:   `uses_local` lists only earlier F IDs; `objects` lists the actually used
277:   global/active local objects. `produces` holds complete local facts
278:   `{id: Fddd, statement, binders, objects, assumptions}`; assumptions lists remaining
279:   local L IDs on which the fact depends. A local fact cannot be used before
280:   its production or outside its assumption/object scope. A paragraph cannot
281:   cite its newly produced F as a previous premise. Formulas to be reused by a
282:   different R must appear in the exported proposition, not only in `produces`.
283: - `introduces`/`discharges`: lists of inference-local assumption IDs (e.g.
284:   `L1`). Temporary assumptions are never proposition vertices. Every introduced
285:   ID is unique in this inference and must be discharged once, no earlier than
286:   introduction. These lists account for prose; Audit A checks the actual
287:   formula, scope, and chosen rule. A correctly closed implication may retain
288:   the assumption in its antecedent. Deleting the ID cannot justify an output.
289: - `applications`: records covering every directly used E/M input, with
290:   `{input, at: Sddd, bindings, hypothesis_checks}`.
291:   `bindings` is a nonempty string spelling out the actual variable/parameter
292:   substitution; it is not a JSON mapping. `hypothesis_checks` is an ordered
293:   list of nonempty strings, one per declared source obligation. For example,
294:   `"bindings": "Set the source parameter a to the current x."` records a
295:   substitution; it does not prove its conditions.
296:   The S paragraph must list
297:   this input in `uses`; only local facts available before that paragraph may
298:   supply application conditions. E applications additionally require
299:   an inference-local unique `id: Addd`; different actual uses of the same E
300:   need separate IDs and records. M may also use explicit A IDs for repeated
301:   instances; a legacy M without `id` uses its input ID as the unique key.
302:   `hypothesis_checks` has one nonempty
303:   explanation for each corresponding source obligation. A hypothesis needs an
304:   actual argument from inputs/H/local proved facts; filling a string is only
305:   an accounting check. Prove substantive normalization bridges as N nodes.
306: 
307: Input-free R nodes are permitted only for explicitly shown calculations or
308: logical/definitional consequences. They are audited proofs, not a fourth kind
309: of trusted source. Transitive inputs need not be repeated unless used directly.
310: 
311: ## Audit record
312: 
313: `audit-a.json` contains `format_version`, `graph_sha256`, `spec_sha256`,
314: `reviewer` (`identity`, `mode`, `independent`, `disclosure`), `target_review`,
315: `definition_reviews`, `source_reviews`, and `inference_reviews`.
316: 
317: Each review contains `verdict: PASS|FAIL|UNVERIFIED`, substantive `notes`, and
318: hashed `evidence`. Inference reviews contain ten separate check review objects:
319: `inputs`, `argument`, `dependency_accounting`, `output`, `scope`, `applicability`,
320: `statement_closure`, `object_closure`, `dependency_closure`, `packet_replay`.
321: Each check has `{verdict, notes, evidence, locations}`. `locations` contains
322: JSON pointers resolving inside that R's actual packet, such as
323: `/inputs/0/statement` or `/inference/argument/1/text`. PASS requires at least
324: one actual inspected location; a boolean/enum alone is insufficient.
325: Every D, every E/M source, every R, and the target must be covered exactly once.
326: Spec input hashes and source evidence are read back; malformed/duplicate JSON
327: keys, missing files, changed bytes, failed verdicts, and stale audit hashes fail.
328: 
329: Use audit `format_version: 3` for all new records. Audit v1/v2 are readable
330: only with historical graph v1 and `--legacy`; they cannot satisfy this contract.
331: Each E source review additionally has `citation_checks`, mapping exactly
332: `literature_identity`, `result_location`, `statement_fidelity`,
333: `context_completeness`, `version_and_eligibility` to separate ordinary review
334: objects `{verdict, notes, evidence}`.
335: Each version-3 inference review additionally has `external_applications`,
336: mapping exactly its E application A IDs to records
337: `{input, verdict, notes, evidence, bindings_review, hypothesis_reviews,
338: conclusion_review, bridges}`. `input` must match A's E; each nested review
339: has `{verdict, notes, evidence}`; the ordered `hypothesis_reviews` list matches
340: all source obligations one for one. `bridges` lists N nodes already in R's
341: direct input list. A bridge string is not a proof of that bridge.
342: 
343: Each inference review also has `replay: {packet_sha256, mode, carrier,
344: prior_exposure, read_materials}`. Modes are `unperformed`,
345: `same_context_diagnostic`, and `fresh_packet_only`. A passing replay/overall
346: inference requires the actual fresh carrier, empty prior proof exposure, and
347: `read_materials` equal to `["packet:<hash>"]` for mathematical input. Skill
348: instructions supply the procedure, not additional mathematics. The hash must
349: match the regenerated packet. Keep traces as evidence; metadata cannot
350: authenticate a claimed identity or prove truthful isolation.
351: 
352: `audit-template` creates only UNVERIFIED reviews, empty check locations and an
353: unperformed replay. It refuses to overwrite an existing output. It does not
354: inherit author notes or old verdicts. `inspect-audit` can inspect this pending
355: record; `check --audit` rejects it. Each PASS must come from actual review.
356: 
357: `check --audit` accepts only fully passing records. `inspect-audit --audit`
358: also validates the completeness and evidence of FAIL/UNVERIFIED records and
359: returns their unresolved review paths; success of inspection is not proof
360: acceptance. Overall PASS with a failed child review never passes acceptance.
361: 
362: Mode `same_context_self_audit` requires `independent: false`. If claiming an
363: independent review, disclose its actual carrier and input boundary; this file
364: does not authenticate identity or prove independence.
365: 
366: ## Local packet
367: 
368: The v2 packet contains `contract_version`, `case_id`, spec/graph hashes,
369: parameters, fixed logic, pins, expanded definitions, complete input/output
370: ports, the current inference, a warning, and `packet_sha256`. Source ports keep
371: applicability obligations and M signatures; primary-document verification is
372: separate. Producer arguments, original-proof locations, source proof text,
373: non-input H and extra ancestor/guard statements are not supplied. Guards must
374: already be direct inputs. The packet intentionally omits the global full target
375: so that its unstated premises cannot become an ambient local hypothesis.
376: 
377: Its digest is SHA256 of UTF-8 canonical JSON (`sort_keys=True`,
378: `ensure_ascii=False`, `separators=(",", ":")`) excluding `packet_sha256`.
379: It is independent of audit-verdict fields, avoiding a circular receipt hash.
380: Packets are generated views and never a second editable proof authority.
381: 
382: ## Mechanical boundaries
383: 
384: The checker validates declared objects, the frozen contract, graph closure,
385: notation-name metadata, citation parity, local-assumption accounting, guarded
386: definition availability, and hash-bound audit coverage. It verifies source
387: checkout/file hashes, not the truth of a source restatement. The printed
388: signature must be obtained from a successful pinned Lean probe and compared by
389: the auditor; an arbitrary string called `signature` is not verification.
390: 
391: The checker cannot establish that a natural-language formula is well typed,
392: that two spellings have the same mathematical meaning, that a hidden theorem
393: was not used, that a local witness did not escape the prose, or that an argument
394: is valid. Those are explicit Audit A obligations. Neither a JSON PASS nor a
395: fabricated complete audit receipt is a mathematical certificate.
396: Numbered-reference diagnostics reject common opaque references, not every
397: possible paraphrase or hidden import. Behavioral tests must actually ask an
398: auditor to review unseen controls; manually prefilled FAIL records only test
399: receipt rejection and must be reported as such.
400: 
401: ## Verified background receipt extension
402: 
403: New receipts declare `background_policy: "verified-background-1"`. Each R review
404: may contain `background_notes`, with fields in background-notes.md. These are
405: actual reviewer judgments, not unverified extra hypotheses. Old consumers must
406: reject unsupported fields rather than silently drop them. The authored graph
407: remains unchanged. A new replay uses `fresh_packet_with_verified_background`
408: and binds `library_evidence` plus its actual material hashes; old strict
409: empty-note records can retain `fresh_packet_only`.
410: 
411: `nl0.validate` returns the note supplement/hash and note count. A packet read
412: from an accepted source includes its notes and the original reviewed-packet
413: hash. This enriched view is not claimed to be the original replay input.
414: Translation binds the supplement in `contract.source.background_supplement_sha256`.
415: 
416: The interface source also retains the complete `background_supplement`, not
417: just its hash. Plan steps list the relevant qualified note IDs, for example
418: `background_notes:["R004.BG001"]`. Workflow freeze checks the paragraph mapping;
419: local Lean packets receive only their selected notes."}

{"path": "nl0/references/external-theorems.md", "total_lines": 128, "start": 1, "end": 128, "start_column": 0, "end_column": 76, "requested_end": 250, "has_more": false, "next_start": null, "next_column": 0, "next_end": null, "text": "1: # External-theorem review: required Audit A standard
2: 
3: Apply this standard to every retained E and every actual use of E in an R.
4: An E keeps the full source theorem; a derived specialization or substantive
5: translation is an internal N. Use the data contract's audit version 2. These
6: are reviewer obligations: a filled record or matching hash cannot establish
7: that a publication or a mathematical assertion is genuine.
8: 
9: ## 1. Document identity
10: 
11: Obtain and read the actual primary document. Match author, title, source kind,
12: publication/release information and exact edition/version to its provenance.
13: Record a traceable original source, retrieval date, local document and hash.
14: A search snippet, model answer, secondary citation, or functioning DOI/URL
15: alone does not establish identity. Books, papers and reliable preprints can
16: qualify; a DOI and journal publication are not universal requirements. Record
17: the source category and grounds for treating it as an admissible source.
18: 
19: For missing originals, follow [ordered source retrieval](source-retrieval.md):
20: arXiv, Google full text, Google DOI discovery and confirmed-DOI Sci-Hub lookup.
21: Use normal browser readback when needed; unresolved access and verification
22: failures remain recorded. Then use the [conditional-source
23: procedure](conditional-sources.md) for unavailable text. Unavailable checks remain UNVERIFIED. A complete explicit
24: secondary statement can support a disclosed conditional run, not an ordinary
25: source-verification PASS.
26: 
27: ## 2. Occurrence of the result
28: 
29: Locate the claimed result in that document and version. Record theorem,
30: lemma, proposition or corollary label and page/section/paragraph/equation as
31: available; unnumbered results require an equally reproducible locator. Retain
32: the relevant primary text or a precise readback record bound to the document.
33: If the cited document merely points elsewhere without actually stating the
34: claimed result, follow and correct the source. An explicitly stated theorem in
35: an authoritative exposition can be cited as such; record its proof attribution
36: without claiming to have audited the referenced proof recursively.
37: Distinguish proved assertions from conjectures, questions, heuristics and
38: numerical observations. Preserve every condition of a conditional result.
39: 
40: ## 3. Statement fidelity
41: 
42: Compare the original full statement with the E statement, explicitly covering
43: objects, domains, scalar fields, spaces, hypotheses, regularity, quantifier
44: order, parameter intervals/endpoints, degeneracies, constant dependencies and
45: the exact conclusion (including a.e./everywhere, topology, uniformity,
46: existence/uniqueness and local/global scope). Record the notation map.
47: Faithful mathematical meaning, not word-for-word copying, is required.
48: Alpha-renaming is allowed. Never turn forall-x-exists-C_x into exists-C-forall-x.
49: 
50: ## 4. Complete context and definitions
51: 
52: Read the surrounding standing assumptions, definitions and conventions that
53: govern the result, including referenced context needed to understand it.
54: Capture any omitted chapter-wide hypotheses and normalization of measures,
55: norms, transforms, signs or scales. Map the source objects to the global D
56: ledger. Do not hide a condition outside the proof graph. A substantive
57: conversion requires an N proof; a renamed symbol is not that proof.
58: 
59: ## 5. Version status and source eligibility
60: 
61: Match every locator and statement to the chosen version. Check available
62: primary version histories, corrections, errata or withdrawal information at
63: the recorded date and scope. Record relevant findings and their effect;
64: explain use of an older version. Absence of a discovered correction is not
65: a guarantee that none exists. Unresolved conflicts remain UNVERIFIED.
66: Never import the target, an unproved project lemma, or a circular dependency
67: as E. Previously proved project modules require an expanded graph or a
68: versioned proof handoff. Do not attribute a combination of sources and a
69: project bridge to a single published theorem. A conjecture-dependent theorem
70: must retain that condition, which must be supplied legitimately at application.
71: 
72: ## 6. Every actual application
73: 
74: Give each actual E application an inference-local A ID. The same E applied
75: twice with different bindings has two A records, even within the same R.
76: For each A inspect the parameter/object bindings, prove every source
77: hypothesis from declared inputs or displayed local derivations, check types,
78: definitions and parameter ranges, identify substantive bridge N nodes, and
79: verify the resulting conclusion supports R's output. Record the evidence for
80: each individual hypothesis. “The theorem applies” is not a mapping.
81: Do not add an unproved hypothesis to close an application. An E passed at its
82: source does not automatically pass at any application site.
83: 
84: ## 7. Ownership of derived work
85: 
86: Put substantive specialization, scaling, change of normalization/domain/space/
87: norm/representation, combinations of sources, and prerequisite lemmas in N.
88: Each N lists its actual E/M/H/earlier-N inputs and its argument. Do not enlarge
89: the quoted theorem. Explicit elementary calculations and logical instantiation
90: may remain inside R; justify them rather than imposing needless graph nodes.
91: 
92: ## 8. Separate decisions and reproducible evidence
93: 
94: For each E write five separate review records: `literature_identity`,
95: `result_location`, `statement_fidelity`, `context_completeness`, and
96: `version_and_eligibility`. Each contains verdict, concrete notes and hashed
97: evidence. The first three must never be merged into one blanket PASS.
98: For each R/A write separate binding, per-hypothesis and conclusion reviews,
99: the source ID and the proved bridge IDs. Record actual reviewer, carrier,
100: shared context and reference material read. Self-audit is not independent.
101: 
102: Use PASS only after the check was performed with adequate evidence; FAIL for
103: an established mismatch/omission/invalid application; UNVERIFIED when necessary
104: evidence is missing. Inaccessible text does not establish nonexistence. An
105: established absence of the claimed result in the cited source is a FAIL.
106: Retain failed records and the exact reason, source location and affected nodes.
107: 
108: ## 9. Acceptance, invalidation and trust boundary
109: 
110: Every retained E check and every application must PASS before the graph can
111: receive DRAFT-AUDIT-PASSED. A load-bearing FAIL blocks acceptance. Source-verification UNVERIFIED can
112: support only the explicitly qualified continuation above; other unresolved
113: mathematical checks still block it. Ordinary whole-proof acceptance requires
114: every retained check to pass. Never replace a
115: missing verification with a historical audit or a Lean build. Changes to the
116: source/version, statement, definitions, bindings or condition proofs invalidate
117: affected reviews; bind the replacement whole receipt to new canonical hashes.
118: 
119: An inaccessible source suspends its citation verification, not the rest of
120: the workflow: continue available checks and explicitly conditional reasoning,
121: then report the unfinished citation checks and the UNVERIFIED overall audit
122: outcome. Descendants can be proved only relative to the explicit E assumption; the
123: whole result cannot receive an unconditional pass based on that source, and source inaccessibility alone is not a finding of mathematical error.
124: 
125: List all external dependencies in the final verdict. This audit is relative
126: to those identified theorems; it does not independently reprove their published
127: proofs or establish a Lean proof of E. Mechanical checks establish record
128: coverage and byte consistency, not authenticity or mathematical correctness."}

{"path": "nl0/references/background-notes.md", "total_lines": 69, "start": 1, "end": 69, "start_column": 0, "end_column": 53, "requested_end": 250, "has_more": false, "next_start": null, "next_column": 0, "next_end": null, "text": "1: # Verified background notes
2: 
3: Audit A's shared acceptance section is the single mathematical authority.
4: `verified-background-1` preserves all ten per-R checks and permits ordinary
5: mathematical compression plus positively checked omitted basic mathlib uses.
6: 
7: ## Admission
8: 
9: An eligible step is correct, routine and local, has all material conditions
10: already available, and needs neither a new hypothesis nor a new core argument.
11: Check mathematical content, not length or familiarity alone. Major tools remain
12: explicit inputs. Wrong quantifiers, unjustified witnesses/limits, hidden project
13: lemmas and inaccessible external citations still block. A source guess is not
14: verification; API difficulty alone is not a mathematical error.
15: 
16: For example, continuity of a pointwise sum follows from the input continuity
17: and the codomain's continuous addition. A reviewer can probe `Continuous.add`
18: and record that application instead of demanding an epsilon-delta proof or an
19: author rewrite. Arbitrary codomains do not supply continuous addition by name.
20: Elementary arithmetic need not display every intermediate chain; a useful short
21: completion can remain an elementary note, with no imported theorem.
22: 
23: ## Record
24: 
25: The reviewer calls `record_background_note` with:
26: 
27: - `id`: local BG001-style ID; `at`: exact `/inference/argument/0/text` pointer;
28: - `kind`: `elementary` or `mathlib`; `fact`: precise statement and conditions;
29: - `grounds`: `{location,reason}` records for actual available inputs,
30:   definitions, parameters or prior in-scope argument;
31: - `justification`: actual correctness/eligibility judgment, not a future TODO;
32: - optional `hint`: short Lean guidance;
33: - for mathlib, `source_id`: the M001-style selector actually checked using
34:   `probe_background`. The controller binds its source/signature/version/evidence;
35:   the reviewer still owns faithful meaning and applicability.
36: 
37: The receipt stores these as `inference_reviews[R].background_notes`; source
38: metadata is case-relative and hash-bound. Existing PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED values
39: remain. PASS with notes describes disclosed routine completion, not unqualified
40: author pre-registration, Lean verification, or success under the old policy.
41: 
42: ## Review and handoff boundary
43: 
44: Local review sees its frozen packet plus logged pinned-mathlib tool responses;
45: it never receives another project proof, author repair history or owner hints.
46: The replay mode and material list disclose this expanded boundary. The actual
47: source probes and tool trace accompany the receipt. Source verification may
48: reuse pinned evidence; it does not require a second model per note.
49: 
50: `nl0.validate` returns the checked note supplement and its hash.
51: `background.effective` creates a derived dependency view adding basic M ports
52: to the appropriate R, without changing author graph bytes or proof paragraphs.
53: At translation entry, retain that supplement and bind its hash in
54: `contract.source.background_supplement_sha256` when notes exist. Include all
55: notes in the local plan; elementary notes need no new theorem root. Mathlib
56: notes become actual library applications, with no new H/axiom/sorry. Audit B
57: checks the same effective inventory and actual Lean closure.
58: 
59: Unchanged note evidence may be inherited with its actual review context. A
60: source extraction changing a consumer with notes requires its affected local
61: review first; the current adapter rejects that case explicitly rather than
62: dropping the notes. Zero extraction and unchanged consumers remain supported.
63: Changed math/conditions return to scoped Audit A; ordinary Lean binding work
64: stays in translation. Historical strict results are preserved, not relabeled.
65: 
66: The interface source also retains the complete `background_supplement`, not
67: just its hash. Plan steps list the relevant qualified note IDs, for example
68: `background_notes:["R004.BG001"]`. Workflow freeze checks the paragraph mapping;
69: local Lean packets receive only their selected notes."}

{"path": "nl0/references/logical-rules.md", "total_lines": 78, "start": 1, "end": 78, "start_column": 0, "end_column": 75, "requested_end": 250, "has_more": false, "next_start": null, "next_column": 0, "next_end": null, "text": "1: # Package local reasoning as true theorem nodes
2: 
3: The main graph has only E/M/H source propositions. A temporary assumption is
4: an argument-local device, never a trusted graph vertex. Every exported N/P is
5: a complete claim under the frozen original context. The audit inspects the
6: local derivation; surface implication syntax alone is insufficient.
7: The complete [neutral JSON example](../templates/quantified-implication-example.md)
8: shows an arbitrary binder, a local antecedent, its discharge and the full
9: quantified output. Follow this accounting rather than silently granting a
10: property in a local object's type.
11: 
12: ## Implication and contradiction
13: 
14: To prove `X -> Y`, introduce X inside one argument, derive Y from the declared
15: inputs, then discharge X into the antecedent. Output `X -> Y`, not Y. To use Y
16: unconditionally later, supply an actually proved X and apply implication
17: elimination. A local X and a proved X are not the same proof object.
18: 
19: To prove `not X`, derive false under local X and discharge X by negation
20: introduction. To prove P by classical contradiction, first produce the complete
21: theorem `not P -> false` (equivalently `not not P`), then apply the fixed
22: classical rule. A single R may combine the operations if every local assumption
23: is accounted for. No classical double-negation elimination under an
24: intuitionistic-only policy.
25: 
26: Example graph: N1 `(not P -> Q)`, N2 `not Q`, R1 outputs N3
27: `(not P -> false)`, R2 outputs P. The argument of R1 locally assumes not P,
28: applies N1 and N2, and closes that assumption. No `not P` root is added.
29: The fallacy “assume P, obtain P, discharge and output P” fails: its valid output
30: would be `P -> P`.
31: 
32: ## Cases
33: 
34: From an already proved `A or B or C`, obtain a common target Q by complete
35: conditional lemmas `A -> Q`, `B -> Q`, `C -> Q`, then disjunction elimination.
36: Alternatively prove `not A`, `not B` and conclude C using the original
37: disjunction. Eliminating A/B without a proved exhaustive disjunction cannot
38: establish C. A branch producing false can produce the common target by false
39: elimination; it does not make false an unconditional source proposition.
40: 
41: Proof bodies may contain all branches locally instead of exporting every
42: branch lemma. Check coverage, identical target/ambient context, and the absence
43: of sibling-branch fact/witness leakage. Introduce/discharge each branch-local
44: assumption in its actual scope.
45: 
46: ## Quantifiers, witnesses, and induction
47: 
48: For universal introduction use an arbitrary variable, then close its binder.
49: It must not occur free in an undischarged extra assumption. If the intended
50: theorem has a premise H(x), retain it in the quantified implication.
51: 
52: For existential elimination start from a proved existence statement, choose a
53: fresh local witness with exactly its stated properties, and prove a conclusion
54: independent of that witness's private identity. A witness depending on n does
55: not yield one witness valid for every n. Do not turn a local witness into a
56: globally available constant without a legitimate, recorded construction.
57: 
58: For natural-number induction prove the base and the complete step
59: `forall n, Q(n) -> Q(n+1)` and use induction to conclude `forall n, Q(n)`.
60: The induction hypothesis is local to the step; there is no circular graph edge.
61: If the step invokes the hypothesis at a transformed point s, include
62: `forall s` in the induction invariant. Well-founded induction needs the exact
63: well-founded relation/decrease justification; the word “induct” is not enough.
64: 
65: ## Local notation
66: 
67: Global symbols are reserved. Local binders can repeat across separate nodes
68: or separate binding scopes in a node, but cannot shadow a global symbol.
69: `sum_{k=1}^N` binds k only in that expression. Source theorem dummy variables
70: are alpha-renamed locally, not registered as a new global object each time.
71: Freshness, witness dependencies, constant uniformity, and binder scope are
72: mathematical audit obligations; a list of names does not verify the formula.
73: In v2, local declarations identify introduction kind/basis and inclusive S
74: start/end positions. An input-bound name needs instantiation; a witness needs
75: an actual existence premise. Local F facts record their complete statement,
76: statement-local binders, used objects and remaining assumptions. Neither a
77: fact nor a chosen witness may escape its scope. The checker accounts for

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority, ultrafast.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

When a submit tool returns stage_complete:true, end your turn immediately. This controller handles subsequent stages; do not keep calling tools or seek a later-stage verdict here. This is a Yui workflow stage. Read the relevant declared Yui rules, preserve the supplied proof route and exact allowed assumptions, and distinguish mathematical review from structural checks.

## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements

Contract version: `nl0-audit-a-8`.

This section is the single authority for what an accepted NL0 must satisfy.
Authoring instructions explain how to meet it; the audit checks these same
requirements. The table IDs also name executable coverage groups. Detailed
definitions in self-containment, logical rules and external-theorem review are
annexes to these requirements, not alternative permission policies.

| ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the original target, every original H, quantifier, domain, range, normalization, endpoint and supplied core proof route. Parameters name ambient data; they cannot hide an H or a desired conclusion. |
| `definitions` | package | original_context_note | Give each global object one complete typed definition and each local object a legitimate scoped introduction. Prove or directly assume every construction guard before use. Defining an object grants none of its properties. |
| `sources` | package | original_context_note | Every selected M/E has an explicit faithful full statement and verified primary/native identity, context and hypotheses. Native typeclass premises are mathematical premises too. Record inaccessible checks as UNVERIFIED; they do not support an unqualified whole-proof pass. |
| `structure` | package | original_context_note | H/E/M are the only proposition roots. Every N/P has one producer, every retained non-H node lies in P's AND dependency closure, and every local proof uses its actual direct inputs. Keep every original H, including an unused H, and report which are unused. An ancestor is not automatically an input. |
| `statement_closure` | closure | output_notes | Every input and exported N/P states all formulas, quantifiers, conditions and semantic identifications needed by its consumers. A map or identity only present in the producer's body is unavailable to another node. Original text, equation labels and external notation cannot supply content. |
| `object_closure` | closure | declaration_check | Reverse-check actual object occurrences against global, statement-bound or local declarations. Types, domains, witness existence, first/last use and parameter dependencies agree. A name in a ledger is not an introduction or existence proof. |
| `dependency_closure` | closure | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Ground factual uses in direct H/E/M/N, earlier in-scope local proofs, permitted elementary reasoning, or positively checked background notes under verified-background-1. Inspect actual prose and conditions; an inventory is not its proof. |
| `inputs` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Direct input statements are faithfully instantiated with compatible objects and assumptions. An internal input exports exactly its stated conclusion, not its producer's unexported facts. |
| `argument` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Establish every output clause at ordinary rigorous natural-language granularity. Check material domains, limits, regularity, uniformity, integrability, signs, constants and degeneracies. Correct routine compression needs no exhaustive elementary calculation chain. |
| `dependency_accounting` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Every explicit input has a real role. Record eligible omitted basic library uses as verified background notes instead of rejecting solely for missing M accounting. No unverified source, extra H, core proof or project lemma can hide in prose, definitions or typeclasses. |
| `output` | inference | output_notes | The proved conclusion is the exact complete exported statement under its stated hypotheses, including all consumer-needed representations and identifications. Never weaken the target or strengthen an H to close the graph. |
| `scope` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Introduce and discharge temporary assumptions inside arguments. Close implications, cases, negations and quantifiers correctly; no witness or local assumption escapes. Original hypotheses remain explicit H inputs. |
| `applicability` | inference | source_application_check | For every actual M/E use, give the exact substitution and a direct input or displayed earlier derivation for every premise, plus any proved bridge to the claimed conclusion. Saying that a condition holds is not grounds for it. |

### Scope of the same requirements

Global review checks the original target/H, source authenticity and complete
graph: H/E/M are its roots, and each N/P has its producer in that graph.
Its source judgments establish identity, full-statement fidelity and source
conditions; they do not re-prove each consumer's application. Its structure
judgment checks the actual AND graph and declared producer/input boundaries,
not whether a later packet reviewer has already returned PASS. Conditional
packet review owns each actual substitution, premise discharge, local proof
and output under those checked source statements. Final acceptance joins
all required source, structure and packet judgments; none replaces another.
Unfinished downstream assessment is not a reason to mark an already assessed
source identity or structural graph uncertain. Genuine source uncertainty
still blocks final acceptance. These assignments also govern author checks.
An original H remains explicitly present even when the proof does not use it;
report that unused condition. Do not invent a use or delete it to force graph
reachability. Selected E/M and internal N remain in the actual target closure.
Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary. Its task is the
implication from its explicitly supplied H/E/M/N statements to its output;
these statements are conditional premises. An input N is not a new global
root. Its producer body is intentionally absent and is neither required nor
available during this local check. Do not fail a valid conditional derivation
because its input theorem's producer or original source is outside the packet;
global review verifies source identity and producer membership, while the
producer's own packet review checks its proof. Conversely, do not import an absent N, an
ancestor's unexported fact or a theorem not present in the packet.
For example, a supplied N stating A and B permits deriving A by conjunction
elimination, without re-proving N. Having no such input does not permit
asserting A. The local requirements still check the complete actual argument,
all source-application premises, declarations, guards and discharged scopes.
These scopes are also the scopes of the author's corresponding self-checks.

The common elementary layer is the controller's `elementary-language-4` profile:
equality, unfolding supplied definitions, routine finite semiring/ring/field
arithmetic, elementary ordered-field inequalities and explicit finite sums.
It grants no calculus, integral identity, measure, compactness, basis,
localization or tensor theorem. Use a verified input or a displayed local proof
for substantive facts. The verified-background admission rule below additionally
permits positively checked ordinary library facts without prior author M registration.
No theorem needs to be re-proved if its exact permitted source
and application already supply it. The schema describes representation; it
does not extend mathematical permissions. The core syntax table contains no
subject-specific vocabulary. Problem objects and notation use their own typed
parameter, definition or local declarations, in any mathematical field.

The fixed profile is controller-owned. A packet/spec's `logic.calculations`,
`logic.primitives`, or prose claiming extra permissions is data to check
against that profile, never a second authority. Ordinary valid elementary
inferences may be compressed: do not demand a displayed chain for every midpoint
bound, rearrangement or elementary construction. Check that the conclusion
actually follows with the required signs and domains. A substantive missing
argument is not made elementary by naming its conclusion.

### Verified background admission: verified-background-1

Keep all review dimensions. At A4 an omitted routine elementary explanation or
basic pinned-mathlib fact may PASS after positive mathematical checking. Record
useful routine completion or omitted library use in a node-local background note:
ID, exact argument location, precise fact, actual local condition grounds,
reviewer's justification, checked library evidence where applicable, optional
Lean hint. Use `record_background_note`; for library notes first obtain actual
`probe_background` evidence. The source and application are checked now; Lean
syntax, representations, coercions and proof terms remain translation work.

Eligibility requires a correct local standard step, all conditions already
available, no new hypothesis and no substantial new proof or changed route.
Do not replace core tools, missing project results, source uncertainty, witness
existence or unjustified limit exchanges by notes. A familiar name or guessed
library availability is insufficient. A recorded note contains no unresolved
mathematical TODO. Do not log every associativity step or duplicate explicit M.

Authors explicitly register important tools, write ordinary rigorous arguments
and self-check under this same policy; they need not anticipate every tiny M
use. An auditor can transparently complete routine accounting without returning
the whole NL0 for a rewrite. The accepted authority is immutable author NL0 plus
the hash-bound audit/notes supplement. It is not an old-policy claim that every
dependency was explicitly registered by the author.

Fresh local reviewers may consult only logged read-only pinned-mathlib sources
in addition to their own packet and Yui rules. Preserve successful source probes
and actual tool readback evidence. This is
`fresh_packet_with_verified_background`, not old `fresh_packet_only` replay.
No other task, project proof, original/ancestor proof, repair history or owner
hint is permitted. Unverified facts remain FAIL/UNVERIFIED as appropriate.
Display PASS with background notes when present, retaining their count. The
supplement is mandatory translation input; none of its facts may become an
unproved Lean assumption. See [background notes](background-notes.md).

A calculation label alone does not establish the existence of a canonical
decomposition, normal form, extremizer, basis or structural identification.
Give the actual construction and grounds for its required properties and
completion, or supply a verified source with its actual application. Before
declaring a mathematical obstruction, check the full quantified definition
and the direction of the claimed bounds. One feasible value alone does not
establish an extremal value. A failed attempted argument is not by itself
evidence against the supplied proof.

Unfolding an explicitly supplied definition and displaying its logical
consequence is a local derivation; it does not need a separate source theorem
merely because that consequence has a familiar name. Conversely, a familiar
name without the required definition, premises and derivation supplies no
fact. Check the actual argument and identify the specific unsupported step;
do not replace that check with a blanket objection to a named result.
Distinguish a genuinely partial construction from an explicitly total
operation: its stated type/convention controls which existence guards are
needed, and totality alone grants no intended analytic property.

Authors construct arguments and their evidence together, then report their
own actual check outcomes. An explicitly unresolved or unperformed check
prevents release as a complete artifact. Finishing a checklist, retrieving a
source, passing a structural gate or asserting that conditions hold proves
none of the mathematical requirements. Audit A remains an independent actual
judgment and can find an omission the author did not recognize.

366: ## Local packet

2: 
3: Apply this standard to every retained E and every actual use of E in an R.
4: An E keeps the full source theorem; a derived specialization or substantive

6: are reviewer obligations: a filled record or matching hash cannot establish
7: that a publication or a mathematical assertion is genuine.
8: 
9: ## 1. Document identity
10: 
11: Obtain and read the actual primary document. Match author, title, source kind,
12: publication/release information and exact edition/version to its provenance.
13: Record a traceable original source, retrieval date, local document and hash.
14: A search snippet, model answer, secondary citation, or functioning DOI/URL
15: alone does not establish identity. Books, papers and reliable preprints can
16: qualify; a DOI and journal publication are not universal requirements. Record
17: the source category and grounds for treating it as an admissible source.
18: 
19: For missing originals, follow [ordered source retrieval](source-retrieval.md):
20: arXiv, Google full text, Google DOI discovery and confirmed-DOI Sci-Hub lookup.
21: Use normal browser readback when needed; unresolved access and verification
22: failures remain recorded. Then use the [conditional-source
23: procedure](conditional-sources.md) for unavailable text. Unavailable checks remain UNVERIFIED. A complete explicit
24: secondary statement can support a disclosed conditional run, not an ordinary
25: source-verification PASS.
26: 
27: ## 2. Occurrence of the result
28: 
29: Locate the claimed result in that document and version. Record theorem,
30: lemma, proposition or corollary label and page/section/paragraph/equation as
31: available; unnumbered results require an equally reproducible locator. Retain
32: the relevant primary text or a precise readback record bound to the document.
33: If the cited document merely points elsewhere without actually stating the
34: claimed result, follow and correct the source. An explicitly stated theorem in
35: an authoritative exposition can be cited as such; record its proof attribution
36: without claiming to have audited the referenced proof recursively.
37: Distinguish proved assertions from conjectures, questions, heuristics and
38: numerical observations. Preserve every condition of a conditional result.
39: 
40: ## 3. Statement fidelity
41: 
42: Compare the original full statement with the E statement, explicitly covering
43: objects, domains, scalar fields, spaces, hypotheses, regularity, quantifier
44: order, parameter intervals/endpoints, degeneracies, constant dependencies and
45: the exact conclusion (including a.e./everywhere, topology, uniformity,
46: existence/uniqueness and local/global scope). Record the notation map.
47: Faithful mathematical meaning, not word-for-word copying, is required.
48: Alpha-renaming is allowed. Never turn forall-x-exists-C_x into exists-C-forall-x.
49: 
50: ## 4. Complete context and definitions
51: 
52: Read the surrounding standing assumptions, definitions and conventions that
53: govern the result, including referenced context needed to understand it.
54: Capture any omitted chapter-wide hypotheses and normalization of measures,
55: norms, transforms, signs or scales. Map the source objects to the global D
56: ledger. Do not hide a condition outside the proof graph. A substantive
57: conversion requires an N proof; a renamed symbol is not that proof.
58: 
59: ## 5. Version status and source eligibility
60: 
61: Match every locator and statement to the chosen version. Check available
62: primary version histories, corrections, errata or withdrawal information at
63: the recorded date and scope. Record relevant findings and their effect;
64: explain use of an older version. Absence of a discovered correction is not
65: a guarantee that none exists. Unresolved conflicts remain UNVERIFIED.
66: Never import the target, an unproved project lemma, or a circular dependency
67: as E. Previously proved project modules require an expanded graph or a
68: versioned proof handoff. Do not attribute a combination of sources and a
69: project bridge to a single published theorem. A conjecture-dependent theorem
70: must retain that condition, which must be supplied legitimately at application.

72: ## 6. Every actual application
73: 
74: Give each actual E application an inference-local A ID. The same E applied
75: twice with different bindings has two A records, even within the same R.
76: For each A inspect the parameter/object bindings, prove every source
77: hypothesis from declared inputs or displayed local derivations, check types,
78: definitions and parameter ranges, identify substantive bridge N nodes, and
79: verify the resulting conclusion supports R's output. Record the evidence for
80: each individual hypothesis. “The theorem applies” is not a mapping.
81: Do not add an unproved hypothesis to close an application. An E passed at its
82: source does not automatically pass at any application site.

84: ## 7. Ownership of derived work
85:

87: norm/representation, combinations of sources, and prerequisite lemmas in N.
88: Each N lists its actual E/M/H/earlier-N inputs and its argument. Do not enlarge

126: to those identified theorems; it does not independently reprove their published
127: proofs or establish a Lean proof of E. Mechanical checks establish record

{"path": "nl0/references/logical-rules.md", "total_lines": 78, "start": 1, "end": 78, "start_column": 0, "end_column": 75, "requested_end": 250, "has_more": false, "next_start": null, "next_column": 0, "next_end": null, "text": "1: # Package local reasoning as true theorem nodes
2: 
3: The main graph has only E/M/H source propositions. A temporary assumption is
4: an argument-local device, never a trusted graph vertex. Every exported N/P is
5: a complete claim under the frozen original context. The audit inspects the
6: local derivation; surface implication syntax alone is insufficient.
7: The complete [neutral JSON example](../templates/quantified-implication-example.md)
8: shows an arbitrary binder, a local antecedent, its discharge and the full
9: quantified output. Follow this accounting rather than silently granting a
10: property in a local object's type.
11: 
12: ## Implication and contradiction
13: 
14: To prove `X -> Y`, introduce X inside one argument, derive Y from the declared
15: inputs, then discharge X into the antecedent. Output `X -> Y`, not Y. To use Y
16: unconditionally later, supply an actually proved X and apply implication
17: elimination. A local X and a proved X are not the same proof object.
18: 
19: To prove `not X`, derive false under local X and discharge X by negation
20: introduction. To prove P by classical contradiction, first produce the complete
21: theorem `not P -> false` (equivalently `not not P`), then apply the fixed
22: classical rule. A single R may combine the operations if every local assumption
23: is accounted for. No classical double-negation elimination under an
24: intuitionistic-only policy.
25: 
26: Example graph: N1 `(not P -> Q)`, N2 `not Q`, R1 outputs N3
27: `(not P -> false)`, R2 outputs P. The argument of R1 locally assumes not P,
28: applies N1 and N2, and closes that assumption. No `not P` root is added.
29: The fallacy “assume P, obtain P, discharge and output P” fails: its valid output
30: would be `P -> P`.
31: 
32: ## Cases
33: 
34: From an already proved `A or B or C`, obtain a common target Q by complete
35: conditional lemmas `A -> Q`, `B -> Q`, `C -> Q`, then disjunction elimination.
36: Alternatively prove `not A`, `not B` and conclude C using the original
37: disjunction. Eliminating A/B without a proved exhaustive disjunction cannot
38: establish C. A branch producing false can produce the common target by false
39: elimination; it does not make false an unconditional source proposition.
40: 
41: Proof bodies may contain all branches locally instead of exporting every
42: branch lemma. Check coverage, identical target/ambient context, and the absence
43: of sibling-branch fact/witness leakage. Introduce/discharge each branch-local
44: assumption in its actual scope.
45: 
46: ## Quantifiers, witnesses, and induction
47: 
48: For universal introduction use an arbitrary variable, then close its binder.
49: It must not occur free in an undischarged extra assumption. If the intended
50: theorem has a premise H(x), retain it in the quantified implication.
51: 
52: For existential elimination start from a proved existence statement, choose a
53: fresh local witness with exactly its stated properties, and prove a conclusion
54: independent of that witness's private identity. A witness depending on n does
55: not yield one witness valid for every n. Do not turn a local witness into a
56: globally available constant without a legitimate, recorded construction.
57: 
58: For natural-number induction prove the base and the complete step
59: `forall n, Q(n) -> Q(n+1)` and use induction to conclude `forall n, Q(n)`.
60: The induction hypothesis is local to the step; there is no circular graph edge.
61: If the step invokes the hypothesis at a transformed point s, include
62: `forall s` in the induction invariant. Well-founded induction needs the exact
63: well-founded relation/decrease justification; the word “induct” is not enough.
64: 
65: ## Local notation
66: 
67: Global symbols are reserved. Local binders can repeat across separate nodes
68: or separate binding scopes in a node, but cannot shadow a global symbol.
69: `sum_{k=1}^N` binds k only in that expression. Source theorem dummy variables
70: are alpha-renamed locally, not registered as a new global object each time.
71: Freshness, witness dependencies, constant uniformity, and binder scope are
72: mathematical audit obligations; a list of names does not verify the formula.
73: In v2, local declarations identify introduction kind/basis and inclusive S
74: start/end positions. An input-bound name needs instantiation; a witness needs
75: an actual existence premise. Local F facts record their complete statement,
76: statement-local binders, used objects and remaining assumptions. Neither a
77: fact nor a chosen witness may escape its scope. The checker accounts for
78: declared scopes; Audit A must also inspect the actual quantifier reasoning."}

## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements

Contract version: `nl0-audit-a-8`.

This section is the single authority for what an accepted NL0 must satisfy.
Authoring instructions explain how to meet it; the audit checks these same
requirements. The table IDs also name executable coverage groups. Detailed
definitions in self-containment, logical rules and external-theorem review are
annexes to these requirements, not alternative permission policies.

| ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the original target, every original H, quantifier, domain, range, normalization, endpoint and supplied core proof route. Parameters name ambient data; they cannot hide an H or a desired conclusion. |
| `definitions` | package | original_context_note | Give each global object one complete typed definition and each local object a legitimate scoped introduction. Prove or directly assume every construction guard before use. Defining an object grants none of its properties. |
| `sources` | package | original_context_note | Every selected M/E has an explicit faithful full statement and verified primary/native identity, context and hypotheses. Native typeclass premises are mathematical premises too. Record inaccessible checks as UNVERIFIED; they do not support an unqualified whole-proof pass. |
| `structure` | package | original_context_note | H/E/M are the only proposition roots. Every N/P has one producer, every retained non-H node lies in P's AND dependency closure, and every local proof uses its actual direct inputs. Keep every original H, including an unused H, and report which are unused. An ancestor is not automatically an input. |
| `statement_closure` | closure | output_notes | Every input and exported N/P states all formulas, quantifiers, conditions and semantic identifications needed by its consumers. A map or identity only present in the producer's body is unavailable to another node. Original text, equation labels and external notation cannot supply content. |
| `object_closure` | closure | declaration_check | Reverse-check actual object occurrences against global, statement-bound or local declarations. Types, domains, witness existence, first/last use and parameter dependencies agree. A name in a ledger is not an introduction or existence proof. |
| `dependency_closure` | closure | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Ground factual uses in direct H/E/M/N, earlier in-scope local proofs, permitted elementary reasoning, or positively checked background notes under verified-background-1. Inspect actual prose and conditions; an inventory is not its proof. |
| `inputs` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Direct input statements are faithfully instantiated with compatible objects and assumptions. An internal input exports exactly its stated conclusion, not its producer's unexported facts. |
| `argument` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Establish every output clause at ordinary rigorous natural-language granularity. Check material domains, limits, regularity, uniformity, integrability, signs, constants and degeneracies. Correct routine compression needs no exhaustive elementary calculation chain. |
| `dependency_accounting` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Every explicit input has a real role. Record eligible omitted basic library uses as verified background notes instead of rejecting solely for missing M accounting. No unverified source, extra H, core proof or project lemma can hide in prose, definitions or typeclasses. |
| `output` | inference | output_notes | The proved conclusion is the exact complete exported statement under its stated hypotheses, including all consumer-needed representations and identifications. Never weaken the target or strengthen an H to close the graph. |
| `scope` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Introduce and discharge temporary assumptions inside arguments. Close implications, cases, negations and quantifiers correctly; no witness or local assumption escapes. Original hypotheses remain explicit H inputs. |
| `applicability` | inference | source_application_check | For every actual M/E use, give the exact substitution and a direct input or displayed earlier derivation for every premise, plus any proved bridge to the claimed conclusion. Saying that a condition holds is not grounds for it. |

### Scope of the same requirements

Global review checks the original target/H, source authenticity and complete
graph: H/E/M are its roots, and each N/P has its producer in that graph.
Its source judgments establish identity, full-statement fidelity and source
conditions; they do not re-prove each consumer's application. Its structure
judgment checks the actual AND graph and declared producer/input boundaries,
not whether a later packet reviewer has already returned PASS. Conditional
packet review owns each actual substitution, premise discharge, local proof
and output under those checked source statements. Final acceptance joins
all required source, structure and packet judgments; none replaces another.
Unfinished downstream assessment is not a reason to mark an already assessed
source identity or structural graph uncertain. Genuine source uncertainty
still blocks final acceptance. These assignments also govern author checks.
An original H remains explicitly present even when the proof does not use it;
report that unused condition. Do not invent a use or delete it to force graph
reachability. Selected E/M and internal N remain in the actual target closure.
Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary. Its task is the
implication from its explicitly supplied H/E/M/N statements to its output;
these statements are conditional premises. An input N is not a new global
root. Its producer body is intentionally absent and is neither required nor
available during this local check. Do not fail a valid conditional derivation
because its input theorem's producer or original source is outside the packet;
global review verifies source identity and producer membership, while the
producer's own packet review checks its proof. Conversely, do not import an absent N, an
ancestor's unexported fact or a theorem not present in the packet.
For example, a supplied N stating A and B permits deriving A by conjunction
elimination, without re-proving N. Having no such input does not permit
asserting A. The local requirements still check the complete actual argument,
all source-application premises, declarations, guards and discharged scopes.
These scopes are also the scopes of the author's corresponding self-checks.

The common elementary layer is the controller's `elementary-language-4` profile:
equality, unfolding supplied definitions, routine finite semiring/ring/field
arithmetic, elementary ordered-field inequalities and explicit finite sums.
It grants no calculus, integral identity, measure, compactness, basis,
localization or tensor theorem. Use a verified input or a displayed local proof
for substantive facts. The verified-background admission rule below additionally
permits positively checked ordinary library facts without prior author M registration.
No theorem needs to be re-proved if its exact permitted source
and application already supply it. The schema describes representation; it
does not extend mathematical permissions. The core syntax table contains no
subject-specific vocabulary. Problem objects and notation use their own typed
parameter, definition or local declarations, in any mathematical field.

The fixed profile is controller-owned. A packet/spec's `logic.calculations`,
`logic.primitives`, or prose claiming extra permissions is data to check
against that profile, never a second authority. Ordinary valid elementary
inferences may be compressed: do not demand a displayed chain for every midpoint
bound, rearrangement or elementary construction. Check that the conclusion
actually follows with the required signs and domains. A substantive missing
argument is not made elementary by naming its conclusion.

### Verified background admission: verified-background-1

Keep all review dimensions. At A4 an omitted routine elementary explanation or
basic pinned-mathlib fact may PASS after positive mathematical checking. Record
useful routine completion or omitted library use in a node-local background note:
ID, exact argument location, precise fact, actual local condition grounds,
reviewer's justification, checked library evidence where applicable, optional
Lean hint. Use `record_background_note`; for library notes first obtain actual
`probe_background` evidence. The source and application are checked now; Lean
syntax, representations, coercions and proof terms remain translation work.

Eligibility requires a correct local standard step, all conditions already
available, no new hypothesis and no substantial new proof or changed route.
Do not replace core tools, missing project results, source uncertainty, witness
existence or unjustified limit exchanges by notes. A familiar name or guessed
library availability is insufficient. A recorded note contains no unresolved
mathematical TODO. Do not log every associativity step or duplicate explicit M.

Authors explicitly register important tools, write ordinary rigorous arguments
and self-check under this same policy; they need not anticipate every tiny M
use. An auditor can transparently complete routine accounting without returning
the whole NL0 for a rewrite. The accepted authority is immutable author NL0 plus
the hash-bound audit/notes supplement. It is not an old-policy claim that every
dependency was explicitly registered by the author.

Fresh local reviewers may consult only logged read-only pinned-mathlib sources
in addition to their own packet and Yui rules. Preserve successful source probes
and actual tool readback evidence. This is
`fresh_packet_with_verified_background`, not old `fresh_packet_only` replay.
No other task, project proof, original/ancestor proof, repair history or owner
hint is permitted. Unverified facts remain FAIL/UNVERIFIED as appropriate.
Display PASS with background notes when present, retaining their count. The
supplement is mandatory translation input; none of its facts may become an
unproved Lean assumption. See [background notes](background-notes.md).

A calculation label alone does not establish the existence of a canonical
decomposition, normal form, extremizer, basis or structural identification.
Give the actual construction and grounds for its required properties and
completion, or supply a verified source with its actual application. Before
declaring a mathematical obstruction, check the full quantified definition
and the direction of the claimed bounds. One feasible value alone does not
establish an extremal value. A failed attempted argument is not by itself
evidence against the supplied proof.

Unfolding an explicitly supplied definition and displaying its logical
consequence is a local derivation; it does not need a separate source theorem
merely because that consequence has a familiar name. Conversely, a familiar
name without the required definition, premises and derivation supplies no
fact. Check the actual argument and identify the specific unsupported step;
do not replace that check with a blanket objection to a named result.
Distinguish a genuinely partial construction from an explicitly total
operation: its stated type/convention controls which existence guards are
needed, and totality alone grants no intended analytic property.

Authors construct arguments and their evidence together, then report their
own actual check outcomes. An explicitly unresolved or unperformed check
prevents release as a complete artifact. Finishing a checklist, retrieving a
source, passing a structural gate or asserting that conditions hold proves
none of the mathematical requirements. Audit A remains an independent actual
judgment and can find an omission the author did not recognize.

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority, ultrafast.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.
